title: ArcCivs four artisan buildings: recipes, item conversion and profession points
assumptions: This is a proposed four-building recipe assessment, not telemetry or evidence of delivery/activation. Low/base/high use 1/10/16 participating cities and 1/5/10 successful completed cycles per city-day. Cycles are illustrative activity cases, not full worker utilization; each recipe transaction is atomic, and missing inputs or output room means zero input consumption, output and profession point.

Sawmill has six mutually exclusive matching-log recipes: 1 OAK_LOG, SPRUCE_LOG, BIRCH_LOG, JUNGLE_LOG, ACACIA_LOG or DARK_OAK_LOG becomes 4 planks of that same wood type. The evaluator reports each wood pair separately as an alternative; do not sum the six rows as though one cycle produced all six plank types.

Blacksmith recipes are alternatives per completed cycle: 3 IRON_INGOT + 2 STICK -> 1 IRON_PICKAXE or IRON_AXE; 1 IRON_INGOT + 2 STICK -> 1 IRON_SHOVEL; 2 IRON_INGOT + 2 STICK -> 1 IRON_HOE. Each recipe alternative is evaluated at the same cycle count to show its own possible output/input demand; these alternatives are not additive and no recipe mix is assumed.

Stonemason converts 4 STONE -> 4 STONE_BRICKS. Library converts 1 BOOK + 1 FEATHER + 1 INK_SAC -> 1 WRITABLE_BOOK. Every output is backed by the specified existing item inputs; these are item conversions, not free item creation or money.

Each building has 1/2/3 worker slots at levels 1/2/3. Producers work at their own workplace on a 60-second interval and complete output into that building’s barrel; the warehouse courier collects it, so the producer no longer returns personally to a common depot. Recipe quantity stays fixed with no level output multiplier. At most one completed cycle per worker per minute is a theoretical 60 cycles/worker-hour or 180 cycles/hour for three workers, not measured throughput; courier routes, storage and missing inputs can reduce realized activity. Removing the former return leg could raise observed production rate, but the effect is unquantified. No offline catch-up is assumed.

These four new professions bring ArcCivs to nine profession tracks alongside the existing five. Each successful cycle adds 1 internal point for its building profession; 10 points advance a level across levels 1..5, and each worker-profession pair caps at 40 lifetime points. Each level above 1 adds 2 max health, with the existing overall cap of 28 unchanged. Other workers, professions and replacements can train independently; no global or weekly network XP cap exists. The 1/5/10-cycle scenarios can be spread across the 1/2/3 workers of the matching building level without exceeding each worker-profession cap in a single week.

The scenarios for each profession are separate workforce allocations, not a combined city forecast. Staffing all four proposed level-3 buildings uses all 12 city worker slots; it cannot be stacked with builder, hall scribe, resident or existing producer slots beyond the unchanged 12-worker city limit. Each building still uses the unchanged 16-building city limit.

Matching held owned tools retain the 10% incoming-damage reduction: AXE for SAWMILL, PICKAXE for BLACKSMITH and STONEMASON, and none for LIBRARY. These rules add no speed or payout multiplier and issue no free tool items. No other item wear, sale or repair quantity is inferred.

The canonical economy inventory continues to treat EconomyShopGUI SELL as current and the SELL-to-contract transition as future. This assessment assigns no sell prices, contract redemption or currency exchange to recipe items, so monetary flows are not quantified or added to the calculator.

Decision represented: enable the four recipes and their internal progression using only their listed existing item inputs, fixed recipe quantities, durable atomic receipts and level-scaled staffing. The result separates each physical item type and internal profession points; it does not model item valuation, exact player recipe choices, online availability, inventory throughput or observed activity. After separately authorized delivery, verify exact input/output receipts, output-space failure, per-worker profession caps, level slots, worker exclusivity and unchanged Vault/token/player-XP totals.
